text:
**For most full-size fridges, a station with about 1,000 Wh covers roughly 12-17 hours, and about 1,500-2,000 Wh covers a full 24 hours.** The sources disagree a bit on the exact figures because fridges differ.

**Three things to check**
1. **Surge output:** This is the spec that most often fails. The compressor spikes at startup, so look for a surge or peak rating of at least ~1,300 W (some large fridges need up to ~2,400 W). Small units under ~1,000 W usually trip at the first start ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Continuous output:** A fridge runs at about 100-250 W, so any ~1,000 W-class station clears this. Add up anything else you'll run at the same time.
3. **Capacity (Wh):** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so average draw is far below the running watts. One test estimates ~41 W average for an efficient 18 cu ft fridge and recommends ~1,400 Wh per day once losses and headroom are included ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).

Also make sure it has a pure sine wave inverter. Reputable LiFePO4 stations do.

**To size it for your fridge:** Take the kWh/year on the yellow EnergyGuide label, then compute kWh × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 for average watts. Next, multiply by 24 hours, divide by 0.85 for inverter losses, and add ~20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Older fridges, ice makers, warm kitchens and frequent door openings push the number up. Keeping the door shut helps a lot.

**Rough guide**
| Outage length | Capacity to look for | Example (prices as listed, they change) |
|---|---|---|
| Several hours to ~half a day | ~1,000-1,150 Wh | [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180), 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W (2,700 W peak), ~$499 |
| ~24 hours | ~1,500-2,100 Wh | [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2), 2,073 Wh, ~$899; [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator), 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W (3,000 W peak), listed at $699.99 after coupon |
| Multi-day | ~3,000 Wh+ | [BLUETTI Elite 300](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-300), 3,014 Wh, ~$1,199 (was on pre-order) |

Avoid the small 300 Wh units (e.g., the Tenergy T320 or ALLPOWERS R600). They're built for phones, laptops and CPAP, not fridges ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/how-much-power-does-a-household-refrigerator-use-watts-startup-surge-energy-per-)).

**Notes**
- Runtime estimates in these sources are modeled, not guaranteed. If your fridge is large, old, or has other loads attached, size up.
- Some links above are affiliate links.
- If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year, how long an outage you want to cover, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
